Issue 13: the first month of the new ferry

Posted on October 2, 2026 by Alice Moreau

The new company has now run the ferry for a month, and the first thing to say is that it has run: every crossing on the winter timetable has sailed, including the two in the storm on the ninth, when the skipper decided that a little spray was not a reason to strand forty schoolchildren on the wrong side of the estuary for the night.

The second thing is that the accounts are open. The board promised to publish them every quarter, and it has gone further and put the first month's figures on the noticeboard at both slipways, with a note in the treasurer's handwriting explaining that the fuel bill is higher than planned because the old boat burns more than anybody had admitted.

The third thing is the timetable itself, which has not changed and will not change before the spring. Several of you have written to ask for a later last crossing on Fridays. The board says it will consider it once the second boat is back from its refit, and I will tell you here as soon as there is anything to tell.

Finally, a correction. In the last issue I wrote that the levy would rise by about the price of two return tickets a year. It is closer to three for the larger houses along the front, which pay on the rateable value, and I am grateful to the reader who wrote in with the arithmetic and a very polite covering note.

Get every issue of The Slipway by email as soon as it is written, a day before it appears here. There is one issue a month, sometimes two when the council is misbehaving, and never anything else: no offers, no partners and no surveys, and every issue ends with a link that takes you off the list at once, without asking why you are going.
